extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal funds (K–12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards that recipients must include in their Title IX grievance procedures (time frames, delays, appeals, sanctions/remedies, standard of evidence, emergency removal, and supportive measures). Aimed at institutions implementing §106.45 grievance processes under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frames for grievance processes
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(v) requires recipients to designate and include in their grievance process what their set time frame will be for each phase of the grievance process (including appeals and any informal resolution process). The grievance process must be concluded in a “reasonably prompt” time frame and may not go on indefinitely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must balance promptness with fairness and accuracy and may set time frames appropriate to their unique educational environment. The Department declined to adopt a single fixed day limit (e.g., 60 days) and instead requires recipients to publish their own reasonably prompt time frames. The requirement applies to informal resolution processes if the recipient offers them, and appeals are mandatory under the final regulations (§106.45(b)(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on delays — temporary, limited, and for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Any short-term delay or extension of a recipient's designated time frames must be for good cause, temporary, and limited in duration; the overall time frame must remain reasonably prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of illustrative (not exhaustive) good cause include concurrent law enforcement activity, absence of parties or witnesses, administrative delay, need for language assistance, or accommodation of disabilities. Recipients retain discretion to determine what constitutes good cause in context, but delays must not be open-ended or protracted. State laws specifying maximum delays may be followed; the regulation permits but does not require recipients to implement short-term delays even for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and explanation when applying delays or extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify the parties whenever the recipient applies a short-term delay or extension and provide an explanation for the delay or extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement promotes predictability and transparency of the grievance process and helps ensure accountability to the parties. Notification is required regardless of the underlying good cause cited for the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to coordinate with concurrent law enforcement (but not dependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations acknowledge that concurrent law enforcement activity may constitute good cause for a short-term delay or extension to allow inclusion of material evidence, but a recipient's grievance process must not be made dependent on law enforcement and may only delay for brief, temporary, limited periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department reasoning: criminal and Title IX processes sometimes overlap and recipients may coordinate to include material law enforcement evidence (e.g., evidence the police plan to release on a specific timeline). However, permitting temporary delays does not permit protracted or indefinite suspension while law enforcement processes (like rape kit processing) continue. Recipients' obligations under Title IX are independent of law enforcement; recipients must still offer supportive measures while any delay is in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include time frames for informal resolution if offered
rubrics_metrics.description: The reasonably prompt time frame requirement applies to informal resolution processes if recipients choose to offer them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients who offer informal resolution must include reasonably prompt time frames for those processes in their grievance procedures, consistent with the requirement to designate set time frames for each phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal authority and supportive measures availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(c) recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis without awaiting conclusion of a grievance process; supportive measures designed to protect safety and deter sexual harassment are available during the pendency of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer supportive measures to complainants (with or without a formal grievance process pending) and must provide supportive measures when refusing to do so would be clearly unreasonable under the circumstances. Supportive measures may be individualized services described in §106.30; remedies may also include those same individualized services but can be disciplinary or punitive and need not avoid burdening the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe or list the range of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(vi) requires a recipient's grievance process to describe the range of disciplinary sanctions and remedies that the recipient may implement following any determination of responsibility, or to list the possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised the provision to permit either a description of the range or a listing of possible disciplinary sanctions and remedies (and to use the term “disciplinary sanctions” consistently). The purpose is transparency and predictability; the list or range need not be exhaustive or exclusive and does not constrain a recipient's discretion to tailor sanctions. Remedies are required to restore or preserve equal access and may include individualized services from §106.30. The regulations do not impose a separate standard of proportionality nor require recipients to list the factors they will or will not consider in issuing sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the term “disciplinary sanctions” for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: For consistency of terminology, the final regulations use “disciplinary sanctions” rather than “sanctions” to clarify that the provision refers to disciplinary actions taken by the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should adopt consistent terminology in their grievance procedures to avoid ambiguity about whether a given action is disciplinary in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies may be disciplinary and need not be non-punitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies designed to restore or preserve equal access to the recipient's education program or activity may include the same individualized services described in §106.30 “supportive measures,” but remedies need not be non-disciplinary or non-punitive and need not avoid burdening the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies are evaluated under the deliberate indifference standard. While remedies aim to ensure a complainant's equal educational access, recipients retain discretion to choose remedies, including ones that may burden respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the standard of evidence to be used and apply it consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(vii) requires a recipient to state whether the standard of evidence to be used to determine responsibility is the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard, and to apply the same standard of evidence to all formal complaints of sexual harassment, including formal complaints against students and against employees (including faculty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen standard must be selected, stated up front in the grievance process, and applied consistently across all formal complaints; recipients may not choose the standard on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and bases for appeal must be specified
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(viii) requires recipients to specify appeal procedures and the bases upon which decisions may be appealed in their grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating appeal procedures promotes parity between parties and understanding of when a decision may be appealed. The final regulations make appeals mandatory (§106.45(b)(8)), and the grievance process must include the procedures for appeals (details and commenters sought specificity about when appeals are permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must avoid open-ended or indefinite grievance processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not permit any recipient's grievance process to go on indefinitely; any delay or extension must be temporary/limited and for good cause, and recipients must designate set time frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes requiring recipients to set their own reasonably prompt time frames increases the likelihood they will meet those time frames. Moving away from a strict single timeline allows for brief, circumstance-driven extensions without creating permanently lingering proceedings. Recipients must also notify parties of delays and justify them in writing.
